Direction: M or O primary → peer secondary
Request FC decimal: Link FC0 reset; FC3 confirmed data FCV=1; FC4 unconfirmed FCV=0
Response FC decimal: Link FC0 ACK; FC1 NACK where applicable
Behavior and failure rules: FT3 length ≤255 including 5 link fields, max wire 292. Reset synchronizes FCB=1; toggle sender only after ACK. Duplicate confirmed FCB: ACK, no upward delivery, no toggle. Retry same frame/FCB; validate address, DIR, CRC, FCV and length. Approved F01-D allows one recovery reset after user-data NACK/DFC=0; fail reset NACK, DFC=1 or second NACK.
Minimum permanent verification: Drop ACK and retransmit; exact once delivery, CRC failures, 292 boundary and all three modes.

Direction: Both transport directions; O→M solicited application response
Behavior and failure rules: IEEE 1815-2012 §4.3 Rules 1-7, §§8.2.1-8.2.2: the link can carry 250 user-data octets, including ONE transport header, so each transport segment carries at most 249 octets of Application Fragment data. Transport FIR/FIN + 6-bit SEQ reassemble a single Application Fragment across many segments; transport segmentation is NOT application fragmentation. Master SHALL put each request into one complete Application Fragment, SHALL support a configurable maximum request fragment size of 249 octets if it can send larger fragments, and SHALL NOT exceed the target Outstation receive-fragment capacity. IEEE requires a Master receiver to accept at least 2048-octet Application Fragments and an Outstation receiver to accept at least 249 octets; actual larger configured capacities, including the selected Host target, require implementation and resource checks. An Object (including FC32/Q5B G120V8 with a potentially large signed certificate) SHALL remain whole within ONE Application Fragment; it MAY span many transport segments but SHALL NOT be split across Application Fragments or independent requests. If the complete object plus APDU/object header, qualifier count and size prefix cannot fit the configured receiver/application size, fail closed or report unsupported capacity, never truncate, silently fragment the object at the Application Layer, or claim the full Q5B maximum works. Outstation may send multiple complete-object Application Fragments in a response; apply per-fragment sequence/CON rules, distinct from Transport SEQ and link CRC. Reject wrong sequence, incomplete reassembly, receiver overflow or invalid duplicate without partial object processing.
Source physical anchors: IEEE §4.3 Rules 1-7 / PDF physical pp80-81 (printed 38-39); §§8.2.1-8.2.2 / PDF pp310-313; §4.6.4 / PDF p132; Annex A.45.8.1-.3 / PDF pp778-782
Minimum permanent verification: Wire exact 249/250 transport-payload boundaries and link CRC; single Master request Application Fragment at configurable 249 limit and >249 when peer capacity supports; large FC32/Q5B G120V8 certificate serialized as ONE complete application object over multiple transport segments, including 6-bit SEQ wrap; verify no split into multiple Application Fragments; reject oversize versus configured receiver including 2048/2049/4096 boundaries, lost/duplicated/out-of-order segments, APDU timeout, transport overflow, bad object length, inappropriate retry and partial delivery; validate multi-fragment Outstation response and CON/FC0 ownership.
Gate / dependencies: D-03;D-06;D-18; CFG-03; CFG-14; PROFILE-055; large-cert RX/TX capacity and permanent process/wire evidence pending

Request qualifier hex: None for plain FC0; authenticated exception V3/Q07 + V9/Q5B
Behavior and failure rules: Match outstanding peer, UNS and 4-bit SEQ. FC0 solicited/unsolicited ownership is distinct; clear only confirmed event set. Plain FC0 is header-only. If response with CON carries G120V1, reply with Aggressive FC0 including V3 first and V9 last.
Minimum permanent verification: Use overlapping solicited/unsolicited sequence numbers; inject duplicate, wrong UNS/SEQ/association, then valid and protected CONFIRM.

Response qualifier hex: 00 / 01, concrete nonzero variation; no GxV0 payload
Behavior and failure rules: 00 uses uint8 start/stop, 01 uint16, 06 no range. FC1 carries selection header only. Return available selected static points using concrete encoding; split noncontiguous ranges. For groups 1/3/30 V0, the selected Table forms are FC1/Q00 or Q01 and distinct FC22/Q06 assignment selector.
Source physical anchors: 4.2.2.7 and 4.4.2 pp74–79,83–86; Table 14-5 pp459–460,463,465; selected Annex A clauses in index
Minimum permanent verification: Exercise Q00/Q01 at 255/256, Q06, sparse points, reversed/truncated range, V0 resolution and excluded variations.
Gate / dependencies: FC22 only on rows that select it; see CLASS-ASSIGN.

Direction: M→O poll; O→M solicited or independently unsolicited
Request FC decimal: 1 for solicited read; none for unsolicited
Behavior and failure rules: 06 all; 07 uint8 count; 08 uint16 count. Responses use uint8 count/index (17) or uint16 count/index (28), concrete variation only. Event precedes static in mixed read; select only requested events and retain each pending event until applicable CONFIRM. FC130 data requires enabled class, single fragment and CON.
Minimum permanent verification: Count-limited reads and both prefixes, missing/wrong CONFIRM, FC130 before/after enable, no duplicate event delivery.
Gate / dependencies: Relative time uses CTO; security statistics use STAT-EVENT.

Response qualifier hex: Echo same qualifier, objects/order and per-point status
Behavior and failure rules: Authorize critical FC3; validate point, code, count and value. Successful selection stores peer, exact request bytes, sequence and deadline. No output execution. Repeated identical SELECT may repeat response; it must not duplicate a later operation. Apply the approved D-07 per-point CROB policy for G12V1. SELECT never actuates; execution requires SA v5, authorization and current interlocks. Preserve generic and analog command behavior.
Minimum permanent verification: For each selected G/V and Q, verify echoed status and zero execution, wrong role/point/value and identical SELECT. Exercise approved D-07 allowed/denied G12V1 point models and verify receiver-side effect, no SELECT execution and no duplicate actuation.

Response qualifier hex: Echo same qualifier, objects/order and per-point status
Behavior and failure rules: Authorize before execution; require exact successful SELECT match, next application sequence and valid timeout. Consume authorization for operation; repeated identical OPERATE can repeat prior response without actuation. Valid CONFIRM does not itself replace SELECT. Apply the approved D-07 per-point CROB policy for G12V1. SELECT never actuates; execution requires SA v5, authorization and current interlocks. Preserve generic and analog command behavior.
Minimum permanent verification: Test matching and mismatched bytes, Q, point and peer, expired selection, CONFIRM between SELECT/OPERATE, and lost response duplicate. Exercise approved D-07 allowed/denied G12V1 point models and verify receiver-side effect, no SELECT execution and no duplicate actuation.

Response qualifier hex: Echo same qualifier and per-point status, error-dependent exceptions
Behavior and failure rules: Authenticate and authorize before invoking control. No SELECT required. No automatic APDU retry; a separately requested new operation advances sequence. Observe receiver state for execution evidence. Apply the approved D-07 per-point CROB policy for G12V1. SELECT never actuates; execution requires SA v5, authorization and current interlocks. Preserve generic and analog command behavior.
Minimum permanent verification: Test both qualifiers and each encoding; loss of response must not trigger a duplicate actuation. Exercise approved D-07 allowed/denied G12V1 point models and verify receiver-side effect, no SELECT execution and no duplicate actuation.

Response FC decimal: None for command; SA FC131 challenge/error when applicable
Behavior and failure rules: No FC129 command response even on failure. For protected FC6 Master waits for possible challenge or uses valid Aggressive envelope; no ordinary control result from send success. Authenticate and authorize before receiver side effect; no automatic APDU retry. Apply the approved D-07 per-point CROB policy for G12V1. SELECT never actuates; execution requires SA v5, authorization and current interlocks. Preserve generic and analog command behavior.
Minimum permanent verification: Test TCP drop/denied/duplicate with receiver count, no FC129, challenge or Aggressive exchange and no plain downgrade. Exercise approved D-07 allowed/denied G12V1 point models and verify receiver-side effect, no SELECT execution and no duplicate actuation.

Behavior and failure rules: Control code plus uint8 Count, uint32 On/Off milliseconds and status. Selected profile permits configured Pulse On with interoperable point model. Control bytes 01 NUL/PULSE_ON, 41 CLOSE/PULSE_ON, 81 TRIP/PULSE_ON only where model/policy permits. Q and clear bits zero; count=1. Owner-approved D-07 (2026-11-11): support CLOSE 0x41 and TRIP 0x81 on configured Complementary points (Latch or Two-output as appropriate). Permit 0x01 NUL/PULSE_ON only on explicitly enabled Activation points; deny on Complementary, disabled or undefined points. Require count=1, no queue/clear, no Pulse Off or Latch OpType. Use the configured safe point pulse duration rather than Master-requested duration; preserve exact request/echo and validate timing semantics. SELECT validates and arms only, never actuates. Authenticate SA v5, authorize the user and recheck interlocks and safe execution conditions before every actuation. Preserve generic library capabilities.
Source physical anchors: IEEE A.8.1 pp547–552 Tables A-1/A-2; Profile pp3,6
Minimum permanent verification: Test 01/41/81 per point eligibility, reserved TCC, queue/clear, count 0/>1 and excluded OpTypes; zero denied actuation. Test 0x41/0x81 on both Complementary models and 0x01 on enabled Activation; deny 0x01 on Complementary/disabled/unknown points, unsupported TCC/OpType, queue/clear, count=0 or >1 and invalid timing/configuration. Check configured pulse duration, no actuation on SELECT, authorization/interlock denial, expired/mismatched selection and duplicate/replay without extra execution. Exercise G12V1 Q17/Q28, FC3/4/5/6 under SA REQUIRED, exact acknowledged echo and no FC129 for FC6; record receiver effects and generic compatibility regression.

Behavior and failure rules: V1 int32, V2 int16, V3 IEEE754 binary32, followed by status octet. Request status zero. Deny RTU V4 and other unselected variations; keep generic library behavior. Enforce configured output range and reject non-finite values for Host actuation.
Minimum permanent verification: Exercise signed extrema and float bit pattern; reject out-of-range, NaN/Inf, V4 under each FC, and unauthorized requests.

Behavior and failure rules: READ returns current 48-bit little-endian ms since Unix epoch. Separate from WRITE and CTO.
Minimum permanent verification: Known clock vector and count 0/2, missing payload, optional Master issue and typed delivery.

Behavior and failure rules: Apply only authenticated, authorized time WRITE. Serial synchronization uses measured delay, network time procedure is separate. Time WRITE no application or link retry.
Minimum permanent verification: Inject clock write callback, reject count 0/2 and malformed time, drop result and verify no retransmit.

Behavior and failure rules: 48-bit epoch ms base precedes dependent G2V3/G4V3 headers within same fragment. V1 synchronized, V2 unsynchronized. Add uint16 ms offset; a new CTO replaces prior context; never reuse across fragments.
Minimum permanent verification: Test 0/65535 offset, sync flag, two CTOs, missing/late CTO and fragment boundary.

Behavior and failure rules: G52V1 uint16 seconds or V2 uint16 milliseconds. Send response immediately, then start restart; SA critical. Master honors advertised quiet period. Apply restart rules independently of IIN-only diagnostic hook.
Minimum permanent verification: Test both delay units, payload rejection, authenticated cold restart and post-restart IIN/SA/integrity/unsolicited sequence.

Behavior and failure rules: Reply contains a single uint16 ms turnaround delay; V1 disallowed for FC23. No retry of request or response at either link or application layer.
Minimum permanent verification: Drop request and response independently and assert zero retransmits; verify exact G52V2 response bytes.

Response qualifier hex: Concrete static/event objects; no G60 payload
Behavior and failure rules: G60V1 selects configured Class 0 static values. V2/V3/V4 select Class 1/2/3 events, respectively; count limits apply only to event classes. Integrity request combines class headers and preserves event-before-static ordering.
Minimum permanent verification: Exercise each class and Q, limits, no G60 data in result, empty class and mixed integrity.

Request qualifier hex: 06 for G60V1–4 followed by selected G1/3/30V0 Q06
Behavior and failure rules: Each class header scopes following point selection headers. V1 removes event class; V2–V4 assign classes 1–3. Validate unsupported and dangling headers and do not broaden Tavanir point selectors based on additional IEEE table entries.
Minimum permanent verification: Test each class, successive class scopes, dangling/unsupported selector, restart retention and subsequent event routing.
Gate / dependencies: FC22 optional critical per Table 7-7; configure per association.

Behavior and failure rules: Enable/disable selected event classes. Do not accept Class 0 as event enable. Both functions critical in SA. Disable stops applicable data transmission according to outstanding confirmation state; preserve buffered events.
Minimum permanent verification: Test individual and combined classes, unauthorized disable, wrong Q, active confirmation and later poll.

Behavior and failure rules: IEEE §4.6.6/§5.1.1.1 startup NULL: FC130, no object/G120V1, FIR=FIN=CON=UNS=1. Confirm FC0 matching UNS/SEQ; repeat NULL until valid CONFIRM, preserve queued events. After restart Master clears IIN1.7 using G80V1, completes SA and integrity as applicable, and re-enables event unsolicited with FC20. Do not originate arbitrary static unsolicited. Contractual discrepancy documented.
Minimum permanent verification: Permanent unit/wire/separate-process TCP: initial NULL exactly no object/G120V1; UNS/SEQ/FIR/FIN/CON and FC0 matching; wrong/late/duplicate confirm; unlimited startup retries until correct confirm; event retention through restart; FC20 after startup; prohibit pre-enable unsolicited events; confirm unsolicited during solicited transaction; Master IIN1.7/SA/G80V1/integrity/FC20 ordering; parse received peer static while local Outstation never emits forbidden restart static; permitted legacy G10V2/G40V2 only when IEEE allows; secure-auth restart/reconnect. Test with actual bytes/sequence and separate Windows TCP peers; no runtime PASS claimed by document edit.

Behavior and failure rules: G80V1 packed status bits are separate from response-header IIN. Do not allow READ selectors to establish WRITE permission.
Minimum permanent verification: Test both selectors and bit packing, invalid index range and raw header IIN comparison.

Behavior and failure rules: Clear DEVICE_RESTART only. Reject other indices or attempts to set the bit. SA session keys first when configured, then authorized WRITE, then integrity and optional unsolicited enable.
Minimum permanent verification: Test 7→0 with Q00; reject 7→1, mixed ranges and Q01 write in selected profile.

Direction: Either Challenger; FC32 M→O, FC131 O→M
Request FC decimal: 32 V1 or V2; 131 V1 or V2 from O
Request qualifier hex: 5B, one object unless V1 trailers in data response
Response FC decimal: 131 V2 to M challenge; 32 V2 to O challenge; original normal result or 131/V7 as applicable
Response qualifier hex: 5B for SA objects; original object-specific Q for normal result
Behavior and failure rules: Bind V1 to exact original APDU, direction, sequence, negotiated MAC and deadline. Outstation challenges with unknown user 0; Master reply supplies its actual user. Master challenges an Outstation response using default user 1. V2 echoes the challenge sequence, identifies the key owner and authenticates challenge APDU then original APDU per Table A-2. Execute held critical APDU only once after successful validation. No normal result to original FC6. A CON response may carry a V1 trailer requesting authenticated CONFIRM.
Minimum permanent verification: Challenge in both directions, wrong user/sequence/direction, lost/late reply, MAC mutation, duplicate critical request and confirmed response exception.

Direction: Original M→O request or O→M data response
Request FC decimal: Original valid request FC including conditional FC0; no generic FC32 substitution
Request qualifier hex: V3 first Q07 count 1, normal body, V9 last Q5B count 1
Response FC decimal: Original FC129/130 for O data; original FC-specific outcome
Response qualifier hex: Envelope V3/Q07 then V9/Q5B around the normal objects
Behavior and failure rules: After challenge history, bind V3 sequence/user and MAC to existing association/session/direction. G120V9 authenticates the whole covered fragment per Annex. Reject missing/misordered/duplicate envelope and replay. Valid V1 in CON response creates special Aggressive FC0 even if ordinary Aggressive disabled.
Minimum permanent verification: First use without Challenge, known vector, repeated/altered MAC and V3/V9 placement; FC0 exception; no delivery before authentication.
Gate / dependencies: D-12; selected receive/issue capability remains required.

Behavior and failure rules: V4 supplies uint16 user, 0 invalid. V5 returns KSQ, user, wrap/MAC IDs, status and challenge, and MAC under current/last valid monitoring key if any. Invalid user reports AUTH_FAIL. V6 uses authenticated last V5 status and pending KSQ; install direction keys only after unwrap and transcript match; Master verifies V5 OK and MAC before use.
Minimum permanent verification: Initial NOT_INIT, unknown user, two users, tampered wrap/status/KSQ, both direction keys, rekey time/count, valid confirmation and late reply.

Behavior and failure rules: RFC3394 wrap with default IV under current Update Key. V6 wraps control and monitoring Session Keys and status transcript in Annex Table A-5 order. AES-256 KEK mandatory selected; IEEE AES-128 interoperability capability separately tracked. Use fresh unpredictable directional keys; 256-bit Host key preference.
Minimum permanent verification: Test RFC3394 known vector, wrong KEK/IV, truncated and stale transcript, RNG failure, key lengths and no partial install.

Direction: M→O error info; O→M protocol error
Response FC decimal: None to FC33; O reports independent FC131/V7 when permitted
Behavior and failure rules: IEEE Annex A.45.7.2.2 reason 5=MAC Algorithm Not Supported; reason 7=Authorization Failed. Fail closed, no MAC downgrade. §7.5.5.7 contradiction retained under P4-OPEN-01; do not emit 5 for authorization denial.
Minimum permanent verification: Test FC33 no ACK, bad role vs unsupported MAC, late or forged error, rate limit and latest-only event. Test with actual bytes/sequence and separate Windows TCP peers; no runtime PASS claimed by document edit.

Response qualifier hex: None on success; V7/Q5B on eligible failure
Behavior and failure rules: IEEE A.45.8 pp778-782: G120V8 is a Master-to-Outstation FC32 (0x20) request and the sole object; Q=0x5B variable length, valid object prefix length <=65535. Wire body begins UINT8 Key Change Method (ASYMMETRIC only, no Method 4), UINT8 Certificate Type (1 ID/X.509v3; 2 Attribute/RFC5755), then the corresponding authority-signed IEC/TS 62351-8 certificate. Master relays authority certificate unchanged; authority is not the Master. For configured Method 68 validate the IEEE-listed id-dsa-with-sha256 certificate signatures; respect the external IEC profile's additional required algorithms without inventing a profile. Validate ASN.1/DER, trust chain, algorithm/method consistency, signatures, issuer, identity/public key (ID cert), holder/preceding ID cert (Attribute cert), certificate validity, roles, allowed operations (Attribute: Delete/Change only), allowed AoR(s), monotonically increasing revision, status-change sequence/monotonic serial, replay and user-association ownership. Apply secure-time rules from Table A-8, including later re-evaluation after trusted time sync. Obey user-status/key-change lifecycle; delete immediately; defer add/role/expiry activation until normative successful key change. Respond using permitted FC131/IIN or eligible FC131/G120V7 errors, without inventing success objects. No conflation with TLS transport PKI. IEEE §7.5.5.5 demands receiver SCS greater than previously received; A.45.10.2.2 says the authority wraps after 0xFFFFFFFF. Preserve receiver anti-replay: reject 0 after max in same authority/user trust epoch; perform explicit, authorized new epoch/credential re-enrollment before exhaustion, not an implicit replay-state reset. For Method 68, Table A-12 input order, DSA-SHA-256 (L=2048,N=256), RSAES-OAEP-2048/SHA256, and canonical DER DSA signature per current crypto provider are selected implementation profile; verify canonical encoding, fail closed, require independent wire vector/peer interop before VERIFIED. No application success-object invented. Validate external trust and the recorded signature profile choice against independent wire fixtures.
Minimum permanent verification: Permanent unit/integration/wire/separate-process TCP Master↔Outstation FC32/Q5B: valid external ID certificate; Attribute after ID; Add/Delete/Change; actual asymmetric Update Key lifecycle; correct FC131/error semantics; invalid authority, bad signature, wrong AoR, wrong holder/user/association, absent ID, Method 4 with V8, bad certificate type, method/signature mismatch, malformed/truncated/oversize ASN.1 and Q5B length, expired/future-dated/revoked according to applicable standards, stale revision/SCS/serial, replay, role escalation, restart/time sync; ensure no state mutation or premature role activation on rejection. Separate fixture CA from configurable production trust, preserve test output + commit SHA. Test with actual bytes/sequence and separate Windows TCP peers; no runtime PASS claimed by document edit.

Behavior and failure rules: V11 method/user name plus Master nonce; V12 returns new KSQ, assigned user and Outstation nonce. Bind to pending user/association/method; deny unknown/expired user with error 11 when permitted.
Minimum permanent verification: Test method/role mismatch, expired name, nonce reflection/replay, truncation and timeout.

Request FC decimal: 32 V13 then V15 (Method 4) or V14 (Method 68); 32 V15 alone for verification
Behavior and failure rules: V13 conveys new protected key. V14 signs ordered Table A-12 input with certified user's private key. V15 confirms new key with Table A-13 MAC and correct direction-specific name; standalone V15 verifies current key. Compare KSQ/user/nonces; no fallback or partial activation.
Minimum permanent verification: Test Method 4 and 68 peer vectors, wrong pairing/order, tampered fields, KSQ/user, confirm loss, replay and old-key continuity.

Behavior and failure rules: Unsigned attribute data type 2 plus length and value. V209 advertises actually supported SA version. V210 reports n per association (18 for IEEE v5), not total across associations.
Minimum permanent verification: Test both response encodings, unknown set, invalid length, V209 omission without verified support and n=18 with multiple associations.

Behavior and failure rules: G121V1 payload flags + little-endian uint16 association ID + uint32 count. Standard point indexes 0..17, optional additional associations in 18-point blocks; ID zero means measured on same association. No statistics aliasing between peers.
Minimum permanent verification: Test each selected request/response header, reserved flags, 16-bit indexes, separate associations and all 18 counters.

Direction: M→O read; O→M solicited or unsolicited
Request qualifier hex: 00/01/06/17/28 for V0 per profile; 06/07/08 for V1/V2
Behavior and failure rules: IEEE §7.6.1.4.2 p284: create a G122 event when counter increment since startup or previous G122 event reaches the configured threshold (delta >= threshold). Threshold max 65535, defaults per Table 7-6; update threshold baseline only when the event occurs; persist monotonic uint32 totals, do not freeze/clear, preserve association and CONFIRM ownership. Validate V1 and V2 encoding, event confirmation, class 1-3 selection and association isolation.
Minimum permanent verification: Test all selected Q, quantity/index width, exact threshold, reset/retention, class/confirm and timestamp provenance. Test with actual bytes/sequence and separate Windows TCP peers; no runtime PASS claimed by document edit.

Behavior and failure rules: TLS 1.2 with mTLS, explicit trust/name verification, no NULL ciphers or silent downgrade. Implement mandatory TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_SHA interoperability capability per IEEE §7.8.2, separately configurable from secure-production ECDHE+AEAD policy. Behavior and failure rules: Index: default threshold / trigger. 0:3 unexpected state message; 1:5 authenticated but unauthorized; 2:5 invalid authentication; 3:3 reply timeout; 4:3 auth-failure rekey; 5:100 sent APDU fragment; 6:100 received APDU fragment; 7:100 challenge RX or Aggressive TX; 8:100 challenge TX or Aggressive RX; 9:10 discard; 10:2 security Error TX; 11:10 Error RX; 12:100 successful authentication; 13:10 Session Key change; 14:5 failed Session Key change; 15:1 Update Key change; 16:1 failed Update Key change; 17:3 restart rekey on Master only (zero on Outstation). Select delta >= configured threshold exactly per §7.6.1.4.2; the §11.9.10.2 'exceeds' phrase does not change the selected trigger. No freeze or clear.

Direction: M→O request; O→M response when function allows

Behavior and failure rules: Keep invalid format/parameter handling distinct from unknown object and unsupported function (IIN2 bits 2,1,0).
